scopeReview: PSO-2.A–C: physical/human factors at different scales and arithmetic, physiological and agricultural density definitions and interpretation. Original hypothetical data; farmer/rural resident distinction explicit. Carrying-capacity consequences and population-composition questions are reserved for later topics.
varietyReview: Four interpreted stimuli combine three distinct ratios, reversed density ranks, a river-corridor pattern and employment change. Seven separate applications address terrain, historical persistence, political/cultural factors, scale and limits of density inferences. All five skills and four keys represented.
repetitionReview: Density measures are new course content; calculation and rank-reversal items test different tasks. Physical, economic, historical, political and cultural influences use different scenarios and do not infer a single cause from a map or temporal association.

questions.correctOption: 200 people/km²; 1,200 people/km² of arable land; 50 farmers/km² of arable land
questions.independentReview: Independently computed population/total120000/600=200, population/arable120000/100=1200 andfarmers/arable5000/100=50. Also checked reversed-denominator distractor5000/600=8.333. All options use explicit units.

questions.correctOption: Country A has lower arithmetic density but higher physiological density.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed A arithmetic200/physiological4000 and B arithmetic400/physiological1000. Both areas are positive and arable<=total, so the reversal is internally coherent.

questions.correctOption: Access to water associated with the river corridor
questions.independentReview: Checked all16 dots lie within6 schematic units ofx50 river, while the study area spansx0..100. This corroborates corridor concentration without proving a cause or universal environmental limit.

questions.correctOption: The expansion of industrial employment in Town P may have affected settlement there.
questions.independentReview: Independently compared P jobs+900/population+6000 and Q0/0. The added population exceeds added jobs, and records are aggregate, so one-to-one employment attribution is unsupported.

questions.correctOption: They can raise the costs of farming and transport, while technology and livelihoods affect the response.
questions.independentReview: Checked that the answer explains influence rather than inevitability. Steep slopes and a short growing season supply plausible constraints, not evidence of cultural uniformity or universal absence.

questions.correctOption: Established housing, institutions and networks can sustain a concentration formed under earlier conditions.
questions.independentReview: Separated the historical origin of concentration from present occupational composition. The correct mechanism is persistence of established systems, not a claim that the port retains all freight.

questions.correctOption: Political decisions directing employment and infrastructure toward a particular location
questions.independentReview: Matched the supplied government action to targeted jobs/infrastructure. The answer does not claim an exact migration total or exclude all physical influences.

questions.correctOption: Population locations or small-area counts within the corridor
questions.independentReview: Identified the missing geographic resolution in a country-wide ratio. Local locations/counts supply within-corridor structure; no specific map projection or exhaustive survey is assumed.

questions.correctOption: X has fewer farmers per unit of arable land; differences in machinery and productivity require additional evidence.
questions.independentReview: Held arable denominator fixed and compared farmer numerators. Tested alternatives by considering different possible yields, nonfarm populations and trade with the same farmer/land ratio.

questions.correctOption: Food availability also depends on yields, trade, access and other conditions not measured by this ratio.
questions.independentReview: Verified the density definition and considered equal ratios with different yields/imports/distribution. That counterexample refutes a necessary shortage while preserving land-pressure relevance.

questions.correctOption: Cultural and social connections influencing population distribution at a local scale
questions.independentReview: Used the explicitly supplied community ties rather than attributing behavior to any real population or a national generalization. Similar physical conditions do not explain the local contrast on their own.
